**1. Observation schedule – 40 observations/month, 3 shifts** | Shift | Approx. # of nurses | % of total nurses | Observations per month | |-------|---------------------|-------------------|------------------------| | Day | 11 (≈34 %) | 34 % | 14 | | Evening | 11 (≈34 %) | 34 % | 14 | | Night | 10 (≈33 %) | 32 % | 12 | *Why this split?* The unit has 32 nurses. We allocate observations in direct proportion to the number of staff on each shift so that every nurse group is represented fairly. The two auditors together will perform 20 observations each month; they can alternate shifts (e.g., Auditor A does Day & Night, Auditor B does Evening) or split them evenly within a shift to avoid bias. **Sample monthly calendar** | Week | Auditor | Shift | Observation slots (time blocks) | |------|---------|-------|---------------------------------| | 1 | A | Day | 08:00‑09:30, 10:15‑11:45 | | 1 | B | Evening | 16:00‑17:30, 18:15‑19:45 | | 2 | A | Night | 22:00‑23:30, 00:15‑01:45 | | … | … | … | … | *Key points for the schedule* - **Random selection** – Within each shift, auditors should pick nurses at random (e.g., using a pre‑printed list or an electronic picker) to avoid “observer effect” bias. - **Time blocks** – Observations are clustered in 1–2 h windows so that auditors can cover the required number without over‑stretching. - **Rotation** – Auditors rotate shifts each week, ensuring every shift is covered by both auditors over a month. --- **2. What each auditor must record for a valid observation** | Item | Description | Why it matters | |------|-------------|----------------| | **Observation ID** | Unique number (e.g., 2026‑08‑01‑A‑03) | Enables traceability | | **Date & Time** | Exact timestamp of the hand‑hygiene event | Needed for trend analysis and shift comparison | | **Shift & Nurse ID** | Shift name + nurse’s badge/shift code | Links compliance to staffing patterns | | **WHO “Five Moments”** | 1) Before patient contact, 2) Before aseptic task, 3) After body‑fluid exposure risk, 4) After patient contact, 5) After contact with surroundings | Core audit categories | | **Hand‑hygiene action observed?** | Yes / No | Primary compliance indicator | | **Product used (if yes)** | Soap & water OR alcohol‑based rub | Helps identify product‑specific gaps | | **Compliance rating** | Compliant / Non‑compliant | Final outcome for the observation | | **Reason for non‑compliance (optional)** | e.g., “time pressure”, “product unavailable” | Provides root‑cause data | | **Observer initials** | Auditor A or B | Accountability | *Validation checklist* 1. **All five fields above must be filled** – an incomplete record is considered invalid. 2. **Observation must be spontaneous** – the auditor should not cue the nurse; the event must occur naturally during routine care. 3. **No duplicate observations** – each observation ID must be unique. --- **3. Presenting monthly results to the unit** | Format | Content | Visual aid | |--------|---------|------------| | **Executive summary (1‑page)** | • Overall compliance %
• Compliance by shift
• Compliance by WHO moment
• Top 3 improvement areas | Bar chart: overall vs. shift; pie chart: moments | | **Detailed dashboard** | • Table of all 40 observations with audit outcomes
• Trend line over the past 6 months (if data available)
• Heat‑map of compliance by moment & shift | Line graph: trend; heat‑map matrix | | **Narrative analysis** | • Interpretation of findings (e.g., “Night shift shows lower compliance after patient contact”)
• Root‑cause insights from non‑compliance reasons
• Action plan (product availability, training focus) | Icons/infographics for action items | | **Unit meeting presentation** | • 5‑minute slide deck summarizing key points
• Interactive Q&A session | Slide deck + live poll on improvement ideas | *Key principles for the presentation* - **Clarity & brevity** – Use simple visuals; avoid jargon. - **Contextualize** – Compare current month to previous months or benchmarks (e.g., national target 80 %). - **Action‑oriented** – End with concrete next steps and assign owners (e.g., “Supply team to ensure ABHR availability on night shift by 15 Sept”). - **Feedback loop** – Invite nurses to comment on barriers; incorporate their suggestions into the action plan. --- ### Quick reference: Observation schedule & audit form | Shift | Auditor | Observations | Sample time slots | |-------|---------|--------------|-------------------| | Day | A | 7 | 08:00‑09:30, 10:15‑11:45 | | Day | B | 7 | 12:00‑13:30, 14:15‑15:45 | | Evening | A | 7 | 16:00‑17:30, 18:15‑19:45 | | Evening | B | 7 | 20:00‑21:30, 22:15‑23:45 | | Night | A | 6 | 22:00‑23:30, 00:15‑01:45 | | Night | B | 6 | 02:00‑03:30, 04:15‑05:45 | *Observation form (digital or paper)* ``` Obs ID: __________ Date/Time: __________ Shift: _________ Nurse ID: __________ WHO Moment: _______ Hand hygiene performed? ___ Yes / No Product used: _______ (if yes) Compliance: ________ (Compliant / Non‑compliant) Reason for non‑compliance: ________________________ Auditor initials: _____ ``` By following this structured schedule, rigorous data capture, and clear reporting, the 24‑bed medical‑surgical unit will strengthen its hand‑hygiene culture and move toward higher compliance rates.
